mission: Make professional artifact design a durable harness concern: preserve semantic truth, derive visual authority, compose intentional scenes, use motion only when it communicates state or continuity, prove the rendered result, and backport repeatable corrections into canonical artifact machinery.

applies_to: other professional artifacts with a visual acceptance surface
scope.presentation_specialization: Presentation work is treated as a sequence of scenes rather than isolated pages when narrative, executive, cinematic, immersive, or reference-led quality is requested.
non_goals: forcing one palette or one cinematic style on every artifact
treating generated scenery as operational evidence
duplicating Drive synchronization or provider publication ownership

principles.rule: Resolve facts, evidence, workflow semantics, and archetype obligations before visual treatment. Styling cannot promote unsupported claims or erase operational meaning.
Use the strongest observed visual authority available. A verified rendered exemplar outranks inferred theme internals or a generic aesthetic default.
For presentations, define each scene's job, dominant message, visual anchor, spatial hierarchy, evidence role, and relationship to adjacent scenes before choosing decorative treatments.

Transitions and reveals must communicate continuity, comparison, drill-down, state change, emphasis, or progression. Motion without a semantic job is decoration and does not satisfy the cinematic gate.

Authentic evidence, privacy-safe derivatives, diagrams, and generated illustrative scenery must remain distinguishable. Illustrative imagery may establish context or metaphor but cannot be presented as proof.
Palette is a semantic layer, not a substitute for composition. Layout, depth, hierarchy, typography, rhythm, imagery, evidence staging, and continuity must work independently of color branding.
A material visual change remains a prototype until the actual artifact is rendered/opened, compared against its authority and rubric, and defects are dispositioned.
When a correction should recur, encode it in the canonical generator, template, spec, profile, validator, or test before treating repeated manual restyling as complete.

required_when: the operator requests cinematic, immersive, cutting-edge, or reference-led presentation quality
a visual exemplar or prior deck is supplied as the quality bar
the deck is an executive narrative where spatial continuity materially improves comprehension

scene_contract.dominant_message: Each frame has one primary takeaway. Supporting text and evidence serve that takeaway rather than competing with it.
scene_contract.visual_anchor: Each frame has a deliberate focal object, evidence card, diagram, metric, or environmental anchor instead of undifferentiated prose.
scene_contract.spatial_layers: Foreground, midground, background, whitespace, blur, scale, and contrast create intentional depth and reading order when the style calls for it.
scene_contract.environment_or_metaphor: Scenery or metaphor can carry the story, but it must be relevant to the concept and remain subordinate to truth-bearing evidence.
scene_contract.evidence_staging: Screenshots, diagrams, photos, and charts are framed, cropped, captioned, and positioned as evidence objects; do not drop them into a scene without hierarchy.
scene_contract.continuity_identity: Elements that represent the same concept across adjacent scenes retain recognizable identity and position/scale lineage where continuity matters.
scene_contract.transition_intent: Every nontrivial transition declares its semantic job such as reveal, compare, drill-down, handoff, branch, merge, zoom, or state change.
scene_contract.density_budget: Do not solve crowding by shrinking type until it becomes technically fit but operationally unreadable. Split the story into additional scenes when needed.
scene_contract.deck_rhythm: Inspect the whole deck as a sequence: vary scene families deliberately while preserving a coherent visual grammar and pacing.
scene_contract.static_fallback: A deck remains coherent when motion is unavailable or exported to static/PDF; no key claim may exist only inside animation.

hard_failures.rule: Text, evidence cards, or shapes collide, clip, overflow, or obscure one another in the target renderer.
A cinematic/reference-led deck falls back to title-plus-prose on an empty canvas when the reference establishes a richer scene grammar.
The artifact changes colors or theme while leaving weak hierarchy, composition, spatial depth, or evidence staging unresolved.
Animation exists only to make the deck move, with no declared semantic transition purpose.
Persistent concepts jump arbitrarily between scenes without an intentional discontinuity.
Generated or decorative imagery is presented in a way that can be mistaken for captured operational evidence.
A slide passes only because type, labels, or evidence were squeezed below practical presentation readability.
Every frame repeats the same card/grid composition despite materially different narrative jobs.

strong_reference_signals: environment establishes story context before labels
evidence is staged inside a deliberate composition
adjacent scenes retain spatial or conceptual continuity
speaker notes can carry scene intent and proof constraints
transitions support narrative state rather than merely switching pages
reference_comparison.anti_copy_rule: Extract mechanics, not project-specific imagery, names, claims, or palette.

upstream_prior_art.mechanic: Stable element identities across adjacent slides enable automatic interpolation and spatial continuity.
Full-frame image/video/color and parallax backgrounds make environmental scene layers first-class presentation primitives.
Animation steps are deliberate presentation state; reusable components/layouts support a coherent design language.
Scene-based animation with realtime preview supports authoring story and motion as one design system.
Transitions are explicit objects between sequences, separating scene content from transition presentation and timing.
Reusable masters, images, scheme colors, and speaker notes provide a deterministic PowerPoint substrate; cinematic semantics remain an upper-layer contract.

must_pass: scene-job and dominant-message inspection for presentation scenes
deck-wide rhythm/contact-sheet inspection when presentation has multiple scenes
static fallback when motion is material
durable backport when repeatability is expected
presentation_cinematic_additional: persistent concepts use stable continuity or intentional discontinuity
each material transition has a semantic job
palette is not the only source of polish
the final frame sequence is inspected as a whole rather than only slide-by-slide

proof_ceiling: Static contract, prompt-fixture, regression, and harness validation can prove that cinematic/product-design requirements are encoded and connected. It cannot prove a particular deck is visually excellent or that PowerPoint/Google Slides renders motion identically; that requires artifact-native render/runtime observation.
